terminal_record.title: White House Press Secretary Says Temple-Rebuilding Talks Had Not Occurred
terminal_record.description_short: At a 2025 White House briefing, Karoline Leavitt said rebuilding the Holy Temple had not come up with Trump.
terminal_record.description_medium: At the October 23, 2025 White House briefing, reporter Jake Turx asked Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt whether rebuilding the Holy Temple in Jerusalem had come up in discussions with President Donald Trump. Turx linked his question to the new ballroom renderings. Leavitt said it had not. This card documents that exchange only; it does not establish a religious motive for the ballroom or a broader Temple-related policy.
terminal_record.description_long: At the October 23, 2025 White House briefing, reporter Jake Turx asked Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt whether rebuilding the Holy Temple in Jerusalem had come up in discussions with President Donald Trump. Turx introduced the question while referring to the new ballroom renderings and saying they had prompted the thought. Leavitt answered that the subject had not come up. This documented exchange is the narrower supported subject for the record. It confirms that a reporter made an association after seeing the renderings and that the press secretary denied prior discussion; it does not establish that Trump proposed or approved a Temple project, that the ballroom had a religious or messianic purpose, or that the administration coordinated with Third Temple organizations. The exchange also does not support the original record’s links to the Abraham Accords, Jared Kushner, Oracle, Larry Ellison, or surveillance technology, so those separate strands are removed. This was a question and answer, not an enacted policy or a finding about private conversations. The stored January 20 date is replaced with October 23, 2025, the date shown on the briefing transcript. The available reporting records Leavitt’s answer but cannot independently establish what may have been discussed privately.

terminal_record.title: Trump Hosts Baltic Leaders and Reaffirms U.S. Partnership
terminal_record.description_short: Trump welcomed Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania’s leaders at an April 3, 2018 summit and publicly reaffirmed U.S. partnership.
terminal_record.description_medium: At a White House working lunch and U.S.-Baltic Centennial Summit on April 3, 2018, President Trump welcomed the leaders of Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania. He congratulated the countries on their independence centennials and publicly affirmed a renewed partnership and U.S. recognition of their sovereignty. The original synopsis’s alleged private remark to aides that the leaders were “all the same” is not substantiated by this public transcript.
terminal_record.description_long: On April 3, 2018, President Donald Trump received the leaders of Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania at the White House for a working lunch and the U.S.-Baltic Centennial Summit. Trump congratulated the three countries on the 100th anniversary of their independence and said he was honored to host them. In his remarks, he said the United States had never ceased recognizing the sovereignty of the three Baltic republics and added, “we never let you down. And we won’t let you down.” He described the summit as renewing a partnership grounded in sovereignty and respect for the rule of law. His remarks also previewed discussions about bilateral trade, investment, and military-equipment purchases. The archived transcript supports this public meeting and the statements made there. It does not include the private “all the same” comment attributed to Trump in the original synopsis, and targeted searches did not corroborate that quotation. This narrowed record preserves the documented summit while removing the unsupported private allegation and the inference that it showed indifference to NATO commitments. The transcript does not record private conversations.

source_fact_map.fact: The archived transcript dates Trump's working-lunch remarks to April 3, 2018.
source_fact_map.source_excerpt:
Remarks by President Trump Before a Working Lunch with Heads of the Baltic States

Issued on: April 3, 2018

PRESIDENT TRUMP: Today, it’s my pleasure to congratulate Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania on the 100th anniversary of their independence. That’s really quite a great achievement, and congratulations. And I’m honored to have you with us in the White House and the Oval Office.

From the very beginning of your countries’ independence, the United States never — and this is, like, never — and I think you know that better than anybody — never ceased to recognize the sovereignty of the three Baltic republics, even though, throughout the years, there’s been a lot of conflict, a lot of problems, a lot of difficulty, and we never let you down. And we won’t let you down.

At today’s U.S.-Baltic Centennial Summit, we’re inaugurating 100 years of renewed partnership among our nations, grounded once more in our shared commitment to independent sovereignty and a total respect of the rule of law.

This afternoon, we will discuss our cooperation on a range of issues, including expanding bilateral trade and investment.
